correctness.rationale: Writing monotone data as nonnegative increments converts the derivative functional to cumulative coefficient tails. The positive-side weights alternate with strictly decreasing magnitude, so every even tail is negative and A_2 is strictly the most negative tail. The exact beta-integral/binomial identity gives sum_j alpha_{m,j}=H_{2m}-H_m, hence A_2=-V_m. The displayed difference formula proves strict growth and the harmonic asymptotic gives 1-log(2). Independent exact-rational replay through m=20 reproduced the tail minimum and constants; the package verifier extends analogous finite checks through m=40, while the proof itself is all-order.

value.rationale: This is a motivated sharp stability boundary for a ubiquitous numerical differentiation family: it identifies exactly when monotone samples can produce the wrong derivative sign, quantifies the worst possible defect at every order, and shows that higher formal order worsens this cone-stability defect.
residual_risks: Older variation-diminishing or positive-linear-functional literature may encode the same cumulative-tail calculation under terminology not surfaced by the searches.

final_claim: For every maximal-order centered first-derivative stencil on 2m+1 equispaced nodes, the exact minimum over bounded nondecreasing sample data is zero for m=1 and minus (M/h) times V_m for m at least two, where V_m=m/(m+1)-(H_{2m}-H_m); the sharp defect increases strictly to 1-log(2), with the displayed one-step extremizers.
limitations: Specific to symmetric equispaced maximal-order first-derivative stencils.
Monotone sample data alone are weaker than smooth-function asymptotics, so the theorem is a finite-stencil inference bound rather than a consistency obstruction.
